name: Eki-Naryn Valley
near: The village of Eki-Naryn (in the valley, at the confluence of the rivers); the town of Naryn is about 44 km to the west (open.kg, Journal of Nomads), ~1 h by taxi (TripAdvisor).
elev: About 2250 m (open.kg); the earlier “over 2000 m” does not contradict this.
short: Eki-Naryn (“two Naryns”) is a wooded valley 44 km east of the town of Naryn, at the confluence of the Big and Small Naryn, with spruce-covered slopes, a yurt camp and trails for walks and horse rides.
desc: The name translates from Kyrgyz as “two Naryns”: this is where the Big and Small Naryn merge to form the Naryn River. The valley, at an elevation of about 2250 m, is covered with coniferous (spruce) forest, surrounded by mountains and alpine jailoo (summer pasture); nearby is the Salkyn-Tor National Park, which protects ibexes, deer, wild boar, bears and the snow leopard (open.kg). In summer locals set up yurts here, graze livestock and make felt; archaeologists have found traces of ancient settlements. Foreigners come here relatively rarely — TripAdvisor calls the valley a quiet and wild corner (4.1/5). A gravel road with switchbacks leads from Naryn; further up the Small Naryn runs a canyon through which you can get to Kochkor — that stretch is a dirt road and dangerous in the dark (mykgstan, 2016).
guide: Eki-Naryn is the best short trip out of Naryn into nature: an hour by taxi and you are in a spruce gorge at the place where the Big and Small Naryn meet. The trails start from the bridge — walk along the river and climb the slope to see the confluence from above. Overnight at Akyl's yurt camp: you can take part in cooking and felt-making workshops here, and the host's sons lead hikes and horse rides. Be careful near the cliffs — there are no railings. If you are driving your own car toward Kochkor through the Small Naryn canyon, go through it only in daylight.
see: The confluence of the Big and Small Naryn; spruce slopes and the river valley; trails from the bridge; summer yurts and pastures; Salkyn-Tor National Park nearby; the Small Naryn canyon upstream.
skip: You have only one day in Naryn and are heading on to Tash-Rabat or Kel-Suu — those places are more striking. You want comfort: conditions at the camp are simple. You are traveling with small children — there are no railings at the cliffs.
diff: Easy: walks around the valley and on the trails from the bridge; horse rides and guided hikes — depending on your level. Be careful near unprotected cliffs.
when: June — September (summer yurts, workshops during the summer school holidays — CBT Kyrgyzstan); in autumn — yellow deciduous trees in the valley (not confirmed). The canyon toward Kochkor is dangerous in bad weather.
hours: An open natural area, with no restrictions or permits. Akyl's yurt camp is seasonal (summer), booking via CBT Kyrgyzstan.
daytime: Morning and evening — soft light on the spruce forests and the river confluence; drive the road through the Small Naryn canyon only in daylight (mykgstan).
how: From Naryn by taxi/car about 1 h (≈44 km) on a gravel road with switchbacks (TripAdvisor, open.kg); shared taxis/marshrutkas (minibuses) from Naryn (Journal of Nomads). Alternative — from Kochkor through the Small Naryn canyon (dirt road, daylight only).
needcar: Yes: a taxi or your own car from Naryn; you can try a shared taxi/marshrutka (minibus) to the village of Eki-Naryn.
self: Yes: no permit needed; get there by taxi or your own car, and walk the trails on your own.
roadtype: Naryn — Eki-Naryn: gravel with switchbacks (TripAdvisor); up the Small Naryn canyon toward Kochkor — a dangerous dirt road, fords, do not drive in the dark (mykgstan, 2016).
traveltime: Naryn — Eki-Naryn about 1 h (TripAdvisor); Bishkek — Naryn ~5–6 h; Bishkek — Eki-Naryn — under 400 km (open.kg).
stay: Akyl's Yurt Camp Eki Naryn (CBT Kyrgyzstan): 10 yurts for up to 50 guests, two dining yurts, toilets and a shower, cooking and felt workshops, guides; +996 770 443 331, cbtkgreservation@gmail.com. Prices are not given in the sources. Also guesthouses in Naryn (CBT Naryn).
net: Not confirmed by operator coverage maps; outages are likely in the valley — ask the camp.
entry: Free: an open natural area, no permits or fees found (entry to Salkyn-Tor National Park is a separate site, its fee was not checked).
transfer: Not confirmed: taxi prices Naryn — Eki-Naryn were not found in the sources. Marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek — Naryn — 600 som (CBT Naryn, 05.2026).
bring: Comfortable shoes for the trails, a windbreaker and a warm layer (≈2250 m), tick and insect repellent for the forest (recommendation), water and a snack, cash for the camp.
warn: There are no railings at the cliffs — watch children (TripAdvisor). The Small Naryn canyon is a dangerous dirt road, do not drive it in the dark (mykgstan). The rivers are fast and cold — do not wade across without experience.
food: At Akyl's camp — home-style Kyrgyz cooking and cooking workshops (CBT Kyrgyzstan): beshbarmak, boorsok, kaymak (editorial).
reviews: TripAdvisor: 4.1/5, 10 reviews, No. 5 of 16 in Naryn (as of 07.10.2026). Google Maps — no unambiguous listing (checked 03.10.2026). Pros — beautiful wild views, quiet, easy trails, horse rides; cons — no railings at the cliffs, remoteness, one negative review about the reception at the yurt camp.

p.sum: Eki-Naryn is a wooded valley at the confluence of the Big and Small Naryn, ≈44 km from Naryn (≈1 h by taxi on gravel with switchbacks); no permit needed. Get to Naryn by the Bishkek — Naryn marshrutka (minibus) (600 som) or by plane (2100 som), then take a shared taxi/marshrutka (minibus) from Naryn or a taxi via CBT Naryn. The base is Akyl's yurt camp (Akyl's Yurt Camp, CBT: +996 770 443 331) with horses and guides; on the way is Salkyn-Tor National Park (entry 20 som). The Small Naryn canyon toward Kochkor is for 4×4 only and in daylight only.
